Question: Let $P$ be a pencil (that is, a one-dimensional linear system) of plane curves of degree $d>2$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$. Assume its base locus (the common intersection of all members of the pencil) consists of simple base points, meaning each base point has multiplicity $1$. For a fixed integer $k$, let $m_k$ denote the number of reducible curves in $P$ whose irreducible components all have degree at most $k$. Which of the following is the strongest valid quantitative estimate for $m_k$ under these assumptions?
Predicted label: 'C'
Predicted text: 'One has $m_k\\le 6$ whenever $d\\ge \\tfrac{7}{2}k(k-1)-2$; equivalently, for sufficiently large $d$, the number of such reducible curves in the pencil cannot exceed $6$.'
Correct label: 'C'
Correct text: 'One has $m_k\\le 6$ whenever $d\\ge \\tfrac{7}{2}k(k-1)-2$; equivalently, for sufficiently large $d$, the number of such reducible curves in the pencil cannot exceed $6$.'
Exact Match: 1.0
